impact: Per Radware: a zero-click email could drive ChatGPT's Deep Research agent to exfiltrate data service-side and, in an advanced stage, implant persistent rules in the agent's memory and propagate to further recipients. Demonstrated vulnerability; no in-the-wild victims reported.
mitigations: Radware frames defenses around treating external content reaching an agent as untrusted, constraining agent memory and actions, and monitoring agent behaviour.
name: ZombieAgent: zero-click indirect prompt injection against OpenAI's Deep Research agent

sources.title: Radware Unveils "ZombieAgent": A Newly Discovered Zero-Click, AI Agent Vulnerability Enabling Silent Takeover and Cloud-Based Data Exfiltration

summary: On 2026-01-08 Radware announced ZombieAgent, a zero-click indirect prompt-injection vulnerability targeting OpenAI's ChatGPT Deep Research agent. Per Radware, a single crafted email could cause the agent to exfiltrate sensitive data autonomously from the service side, and an advanced stage could implant malicious rules into the agent's long-term memory or working notes to establish persistence without re-engaging the target, executing hidden actions whenever the agent is used and potentially propagating to further recipients. Radware presents it as building on its earlier ShadowLeak research. The announcement is a vendor disclosure describing a demonstrated vulnerability rather than an observed in-the-wild attack, and is catalogued as an agent-hijack prompt-injection product vulnerability.
